question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Sister-clone splitting to quantify heritability of AP-1 state
ideas.description: Barcode a clonal population, split it into sister subclones after a defined number of divisions, and compare AP-1 reporter activity and AP-1 target-gene expression between sisters versus random pairs. The intraclass correlation as a function of elapsed divisions directly yields the memory half-life of the AP-1 state and separates true heredity from transient, stimulus-driven fluctuation.

ideas.title: Washout-and-rechallenge priming assay
ideas.description: Transiently induce AP-1 (growth factor, optogenetic FOS/JUN dimerization, or an inducible construct), wash out, wait for AP-1 protein and transcript levels to return to baseline, then re-stimulate and measure response amplitude and kinetics. A faster or larger secondary response in previously stimulated cells—when current AP-1 levels are indistinguishable—is the cleanest functional signature of stored memory rather than persistent signaling.

ideas.title: Decoupling stored chromatin state from ongoing AP-1 activity by acute degron depletion
ideas.description: Use a dTAG/auxin degron on FOS and JUN family members to acutely remove AP-1 protein for hours to days, then restore it, measuring enhancer accessibility (ATAC) and target expression before, during, and after. If the pre-depletion enhancer landscape is re-established in the same cells, the memory is carried by something other than AP-1 occupancy itself; if it resets to a naive state, AP-1 occupancy is the memory.

ideas.title: Prospective sorting plus retrospective lineage tracing of AP-1-high cells
ideas.description: Sort AP-1-reporter-high and -low cells from a barcoded population, let each grow out for several weeks, then measure both the reporter distribution and a functional fate (e.g., drug survival or invasion) in the progeny. Combining this with barcode recovery lets you ask whether a given clone's AP-1 state at time zero predicts its fate at time T, which is the operational definition of a memory mechanism.

ideas.title: Hysteresis and bistability mapping of the AP-1 dose response
ideas.description: Expose cells to a graded series of stimulus doses from below and from above (stepping up from zero versus stepping down from saturating stimulus) and measure single-cell AP-1 activity at matched steady-state doses. Overlapping curves indicate a passive relay; a hysteresis loop with a bistable regime would show AP-1 is wired as a self-sustaining memory switch, and mutating AP-1 motifs in FOS/JUN's own regulatory elements should collapse the loop.

candidates: Lineage-barcode twin-clone assay: split barcoded clones, measure AP-1 reporter/target expression in sister subclones to quantify heritability across many divisions
Live-cell AP-1 transcriptional reporter (TRE-destabilized fluorophore) with long-term tracking to measure autocorrelation time of AP-1 activity relative to cell cycle
Retrospective lineage tracing (Rewind-style): sort high- vs low-AP-1 cells, grow out, and ask whether their progeny retain the state weeks later
Single-cell multiome (ATAC + RNA) across time to test whether AP-1 motif accessibility precedes and outlasts AP-1 transcript expression
Degron-mediated acute depletion of FOS/JUN followed by washout: does the prior chromatin/expression state recover (memory) or reset (no memory)?
Transient optogenetic or chemical AP-1 induction, then washout, then re-challenge to test for faster/stronger secondary response (priming memory)
Pulse-chase of AP-1 pioneer-driven enhancer accessibility with ATAC after stimulus removal, measuring enhancer closure half-lives genome-wide
Mitotic bookmarking test: live imaging and ChIP/CUT&RUN of FOS/JUN on mitotic chromatin, plus mitotic-retention mutants
Nucleosome/epigenome editing: dCas9-recruited AP-1 domain at a single enhancer, then release, to test self-sustaining accessibility
Test for AP-1 autoregulatory feedback loop (FOS/JUN binding their own promoters) as a bistability mechanism using motif mutation
Mathematical bistability test: dose-response hysteresis of AP-1 activity to graded stimulus up and down
Single-cell protein half-life measurement of FOS/JUN (SunTag/pulse-chase) to ask whether protein stability alone can explain state persistence
Correlate AP-1 state with functional memory readout: does pre-existing AP-1-high state predict drug-resistant or metastatic fate in barcoded populations?
Serial transplantation / serial passaging of AP-1-high sorted cells in vivo to test persistence of the state outside culture
Perturb candidate memory carriers (BRD4, p300, SWI/SNF, H3K27ac, DNA methylation) and ask which abolishes AP-1 state heritability
Single-molecule FISH for FOS/JUN nascent transcription in sister-cell pairs immediately after division (memory vs. shared cytoplasm confounds)
Cell-cycle-arrested versus dividing cells: does AP-1 state persistence require or survive DNA replication?
CRISPR screen for genes whose loss collapses AP-1 state heterogeneity or erases memory after stimulus washout
Compare AP-1 memory across cell types / species orthologs to test generality and identify conserved enhancer architectures
Integrate published scATAC atlases to test whether AP-1 motif accessibility marks cell-state transitions better than lineage TF motifs
Spatial transcriptomics of tissue to test whether AP-1-high cells occur in clonal/spatially contiguous patches (indicating inherited state)
Measure AP-1 target enhancer accessibility in single cells with and without transcription blockade to separate ongoing signaling from stored state
Design synthetic AP-1-responsive circuits with and without feedback to test sufficiency of AP-1 for making a memory module
Allele-specific analysis in hybrid cells: is AP-1 enhancer accessibility cis-heritable at one allele independent of the other
Reconstitute memory in vitro: nucleosome arrays plus AP-1 to test whether AP-1 alone maintains accessibility through replication
